strongest_confirmed_findings: Q2 revenue was $1.065B; 87.8% was product revenue and one non-related customer represented 73%, about $777.7M on the rounded disclosed share.
Nebius disclosed up to $2.6B of service fees for about 250 guaranteed generation MW over three ten-year phases: a $1.04M per guaranteed generation MW-year aggregate upper bound.
The corresponding upper bound is $0.793M per installed generation MW-year; the 250/328 guaranteed-to-installed ratio is 76.2% and is not PUE, availability or utilization.
Bloom's Fund JV maximum loss was $68.8M and commitments were $77.3M at June 30; project creditors have no general recourse beyond committed contributions.
investable_read_through: Bloom is monetizing urgent AI power demand with measurable supplier economics, but the current revenue surge is product-heavy and highly concentrated. Third-party project finance limits direct current Fund JV exposure and first-half operating cash flow was positive, yet delivery acceptance, financing affiliate execution, fuel/pass-through terms and warranty performance remain the decisive earnings-quality variables.
contradictions_to_prior_assumptions: The Brookfield $25B figure is a financing framework, not Bloom revenue, RPO or debt.
Project Jupiter's up-to-2.45GW and Oracle's up-to-2.8GW are generation-capacity announcements, not IT MW, active capacity or PUE evidence.
Bloom is not presently a recurring-utility pure play: 87.8% of Q2 revenue was product and electricity revenue was only $9.951M.
Supplier PUE is not_applicable; customer operational PUE and effective utilized IT MW are not_disclosed.
unresolved_questions: Nebius phase MW, commercial-operation dates, fee commencement, fuel/escalation/pass-through terms, performance guarantees and realized revenue by phase.
Which project-finance affiliate or end user drove the 73% Q2 customer concentration and how repeatable the product-revenue cohort is.
Tax-equity, senior-debt, collateral, replacement and sponsor-recourse terms for the $1.7B Nebius project financing.
Matched facility energy, IT energy, physical utilization and compute-revenue perimeter at Nebius and Oracle sites.
